title: Private installer: implement `backup create` command (manifest + integrity verification)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Private Day-2 Ops: Backup/Restore + DR Toolkit
description:
Goal
Add a supported `backup create` command to the Redwood Private installer tooling. This command produces a deterministic backup artifact and a machine-readable manifest, and performs integrity verification before reporting success.

Context
This is part of the Private Day-2 Backup/Restore + DR toolkit. Customers and SE/SRE need a repeatable way to capture control-plane state/config in a consistent manner across VPC and on-prem installs, including constrained/air-gapped environments.

User story
As an operator of a Redwood Private control plane, I can run `redwood-private backup create ...` to generate an encrypted backup artifact and a manifest with enough metadata to verify and later restore it deterministically.

Non-goals (explicit)
- Implementing full restore flow (tracked in ENG-9822).
- Designing/implementing KMS envelope encryption provider interface (tracked in ENG-9823). This ticket should integrate with the interface once available, but may ship with a local key provider for dev/test.
- Kubernetes/Velero resource backup orchestration beyond capturing installer-known config inputs (tracked in docs/integration guidance).

Acceptance criteria
1) CLI surface
- `redwood-private backup create` exists in private installer.
- Supports specifying output target:
  - local filesystem path (default)
  - object storage URI (if configured; initial support may be “upload hook” invoked by wrapper script)
- Supports `--namespace` / `--context` (kubeconfig) selection.
- Supports `--include`/`--exclude` flags for component groups (initially: control-plane state + config + release metadata; avoid secrets material).
- Supports `--dry-run` that prints resolved inventory and planned actions without writing artifacts.

2) Artifact format
- Produces:
  a) a manifest file (JSON or YAML) with:
    - backup_format_version
    - created_at timestamp
    - platform_version (control plane)
    - installer_version
    - cluster identifier hints (cluster name, region, provider if known)
    - included components list
    - artifact filenames
    - hash algorithm and per-file checksums
    - encryption metadata (provider, key ID/reference, algorithm)
  b) a single backup payload (tarball) that is encrypted-at-rest (implementation details depend on ENG-9823; for this ticket, ensure the payload is encryptable and never written unencrypted to disk if encryption enabled).
- Deterministic packaging order (stable tar ordering, normalized paths, normalized metadata where feasible).

3) Integrity verification
- After writing the payload, compute checksum(s) and write them to the manifest.
- Re-open the written payload and re-hash to confirm the checksum matches before returning exit code 0.
- Print a short “verification summary” to stdout (artifact size, checksum prefix, manifest path).

4) Logging + exit codes
- Human-readable progress output.
- Structured log line(s) suitable for ingestion (at least: event=backup_create_started/completed/failed, duration_ms, bytes_written, error_category).
- Non-zero exit code on failure; error messages must include operator action hints.

5) Tests
- Unit tests for manifest generation and checksum verification.
- Integration-ish test (can be in CI) that runs `backup create` against a local/dev control plane stub and validates artifacts exist and are self-consistent.

Implementation notes / design sketch
- Introduce internal package `backup` in installer repo:
  - Inventory builder: determines what to collect (installer-known config, Helm values, control-plane DB snapshots hook, etc.).
  - Writer: streams content into tar builder; ensure stable order.
  - Encryptor: interface to be aligned with ENG-9823. Default implementation can be “local key” for non-prod.
  - Verifier: checksum computation + re-read verification.
- Manifest should be written last and include the final checksums.
- Avoid including secret material. Prefer references (secret names, external secret IDs) and configuration hashes. Any accidental inclusion of Kubernetes Secret objects must be blocked by default.

Open questions
- What is the minimum set of control-plane state to treat as “required” vs “optional” for successful restore? (Sync with Ethan/Michael and runbook draft.)
- How to represent “externalized” dependencies in manifest (e.g., S3 bucket for audit logs, external DB endpoints)? (Probably: include as references with warning that external systems must be backed up separately.)

Links
- PM requirements: sources/linear/product-management/PM-418-private-day2-backup-restore-requirements.json
- Related:
  - ENG-9822 implement restore apply workflow
  - ENG-9823 KMS envelope encryption
  - ENG-9830 compatibility matrix + migrations
- Expected follow-on PR(s) for this ticket: sources/github/redwood-private-installer/pr-482-add-backup-create-command.json

Rollout / supportability
- Behind a feature flag `private.backupRestore.enabled` until docs/runbooks land.
- Must be safe to run multiple times; should not mutate cluster state aside from any quiesce hooks explicitly documented.

Definition of done
- Merged PR, CLI available in nightly build.
- Manifest schema documented (inline `--help` + README snippet).
- Security review sign-off on “no secrets material” guarantee (or documented exception + mitigation).
comments: 2025-01-22 — Ethan Park: Marking as P0. Customer calls (FinBank/MedData) are explicitly asking for a supported backup command with integrity verification. Keep scope tight: create command + manifest + verify; restore is separate.

2025-01-24 — Benji Okafor: Proposed manifest fields (backup_format_version, platform/installer versions, included components, checksums, encryption metadata). Will default to writing artifacts to local path; upload can be wrapper-script for Phase 1. Need to ensure deterministic tar ordering; I’ll sort entries and normalize paths.

2025-01-27 — Hanae Suzuki (security): Please ensure we never serialize K8s Secret objects into the tarball. If we need references, include names/UIDs only. Also add an explicit manifest field `contains_secret_material=false` and fail fast if any secret-like data is detected.

2025-01-29 — Michael Nguyen: For control-plane state snapshot hook, let’s implement as a pluggable “collector” interface. In Phase 1 we can snapshot the config DB via existing admin endpoint (if present) or dump the postgres logical backup from the control-plane pod. We need a clear boundary: this ticket should only wire the hook; don’t overbuild migrations here.

2025-02-03 — Connor O'Brien: Release packaging note: artifact + manifest must have stable naming and include installer version in filename to help offline bundles. Please add `--output-dir` and ensure filenames are deterministic. Also, ensure backup create prints paths so our automated smoke tests can pick them up.

2025-02-05 — Benji Okafor: Implementation landed behind feature flag. Added checksum verification by re-reading the written payload. For encryption, current default is local key provider in non-prod; will swap to KMS provider once ENG-9823 merges. Added structured logs: backup_create_started/completed/failed w/ duration_ms and bytes_written.

2025-02-07 — Sean Gallagher: Can we standardize error categories for alerting? e.g., PERMISSION_DENIED, STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, SNAPSHOT_FAILED, VERIFY_FAILED. Please include in logs so SRE can build dashboards later.

2025-02-10 — Benji Okafor: Added error_category mapping and ensured non-zero exit codes. Also added `--dry-run` to print resolved inventory and collector list. Unit tests cover manifest + checksum verification; CI job runs `backup create` against dev harness.

2025-02-12 — Ethan Park: Review: looks good. One request: ensure tar entries use normalized uid/gid + mtime to improve determinism. Also add manifest field for `cluster_id_hint` if available from installer config.
2025-02-14 — Benji Okafor: Addressed determinism feedback (normalized metadata). Added cluster_id_hint from installer config when present. Ready to merge pending security sign-off.

2025-02-18 — Marcus Lin: Security sign-off conditional on: (1) default behavior excludes secret material; (2) any detected Secret objects abort the backup with explicit remediation; (3) docs mention that external secret stores are out of scope and must be backed up separately. Approved for merge with these conditions met.
